solution:
"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/closest-divisors/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

1362. Closest Divisors

Given an integer num, find the closest two integers in absolute difference whose product equals num + 1 or num + 2.

Return the two integers in any order.

Example 1:

Input: num = 8
Output: [3,3]
Explanation: For num + 1 = 9, the closest divisors are 3 & 3, for num + 2 = 10, the closest divisors are 2 & 5, hence 3 & 3 is chosen.

Example 2:

Input: num = 123
Output: [5,25]

Example 3:

Input: num = 999
Output: [25,40]

Constraints:

    1 <= num <= 10^9
"""


class Solution:
    def closestDivisors(self, num: int) -> List[int]:
        def find_closest_pair(x: int) -> List[int]:
            root = int(sqrt(x))
            for i in range(root, 0, -1):
                if x % i == 0:
                    return [i, x // i]
            return [1, x]

        pair1 = find_closest_pair(num + 1)
        pair2 = find_closest_pair(num + 2)

        if abs(pair1[0] - pair1[1]) <= abs(pair2[0] - pair2[1]):
            return pair1
        else:
            return pair2


sol = Solution()

print(sol.closestDivisors(8))  # [3,3]

assert sol.closestDivisors(8) == [3, 3]
assert sol.closestDivisors(123) == [5, 25]
assert sol.closestDivisors(999) == [25, 40]

assert sol.closestDivisors(1) == [1, 2]
assert sol.closestDivisors(2) == [2, 2]
assert sol.closestDivisors(3) == [2, 2]
assert sol.closestDivisors(10**9 - 2) == [31250, 32000]
assert sol.closestDivisors(10**9 - 1) == [31250, 32000]
assert sol.closestDivisors(10**9) == [23658, 42269]
assert sol.closestDivisors(15) == [4, 4]
assert sol.closestDivisors(16) == [3, 6]
assert sol.closestDivisors(17) == [3, 6]
assert sol.closestDivisors(24) == [5, 5]
assert sol.closestDivisors(25) == [3, 9]
assert sol.closestDivisors(26) == [4, 7]
